C0001.d: C0001 concerns the first traction control valve of hydraulic channel A, usually one of the two brake circuits in the ABS/ESC modulator. To brake a spinning drive wheel without driver input, a TCS-capable modulator carries an extra isolation valve and priming valve per circuit: the normally open isolation valve closes off the master cylinder, while the normally closed priming valve opens so the pump can draw fluid and
c: Corroded or chafed wiring to the modulator

C0002.d: C0002 points to the second traction control valve of channel A. Together with valve 1 it forms the valve pair a TCS modulator adds to each brake circuit: an isolation valve that cuts the circuit off from the master cylinder and a priming valve that opens the path from the master cylinder to the return pump, so pressure can rise at a driven wheel while the pedal is released.
c: Corroded or chafed wiring to the modulator

C0003.d: C0003 is the counterpart of C0001 in channel B, the second brake circuit of the modulator. A pump patent for such units shows the layout plainly: two normally open isolation valves and two normally closed priming valves, one of each per circuit, operated by the control unit alongside the apply and release valves when traction control intervenes.
c: Corroded or chafed wiring to the modulator

C0004.d: C0004 completes the set with the second traction control valve of channel B. During an intervention the module closes the isolation valve and opens the priming valve of the circuit concerned so the pump can supply pressure to a wheel that is spinning; afterwards both return to rest so the driver's pedal again acts through the master cylinder.
c: Corroded or chafed wiring to the modulator

C0010.d: Covers the left front inlet (apply) solenoid valve of the ABS hydraulic modulator. During ABS, traction or stability control the module closes this valve to isolate the left front brake circuit from the master cylinder and hold wheel pressure, then opens it to let pressure back in.
c: Inlet valve coil open or shorted
Brake control module fault or false setting

C0011.d: Covers the left front outlet (release) solenoid valve of the ABS hydraulic modulator. This valve opens to dump brake fluid from the left front caliper into the low-pressure accumulator so the module can reduce wheel pressure during an ABS or stability event, then closes to allow reapply.
c: Outlet valve coil open or shorted

C0012.d: Set when the ABS modulator cannot release pressure at the left front wheel within the expected time during a control cycle. Rather than a pure electrical fault it is a performance or plausibility code: after the module commands the left front outlet valve to dump pressure, it expects wheel speed to recover and pressure to fall; if the release takes longer than the calibrated limit the module concludes the hydraulic p
s: Extended or firm pedal during hard braking
c: Restricted hydraulic path or contaminated fluid
Pump or accumulator cannot accept fluid

C0014.d: Covers the right front inlet (apply) solenoid valve of the ABS hydraulic modulator, the mirror of C0010 on the right front corner. The module closes this valve to isolate the right front brake circuit and hold wheel pressure during ABS, traction or stability control, then opens it to reapply pressure from the master cylinder or pump.
c: Inlet valve coil open or shorted

C0015.d: Covers the right front outlet (release) solenoid valve of the ABS hydraulic modulator, the release counterpart to inlet valve C0014. It opens to dump brake fluid from the right front caliper into the low-pressure accumulator so wheel pressure can fall during an ABS or stability cycle, then closes for reapply.
c: Outlet valve coil open or shorted

C0016.d: Set when the ABS modulator cannot release pressure at the right front wheel within the expected time during a control cycle, the right front equivalent of C0012. After commanding the right front outlet valve to dump pressure the module expects wheel speed to recover and line pressure to fall; if the release exceeds the calibrated time limit it infers a sticking valve, a restricted hydraulic path or an accumulator/pum
s: Extended or firm pedal during hard braking
c: Restricted hydraulic path or contaminated fluid
Pump or accumulator cannot accept fluid

C0018.d: Covers the left rear inlet (apply) solenoid valve of the ABS hydraulic modulator, the rear-axle counterpart of C0010. The module closes this valve to isolate the left rear brake circuit and hold wheel pressure during ABS, traction or stability control, then opens it to reapply pressure.
c: Inlet valve coil open or shorted

C0019.d: Covers the left rear outlet (release) solenoid valve of the ABS hydraulic modulator, the release counterpart to inlet valve C0018. It opens to dump brake fluid from the left rear caliper or wheel cylinder into the low-pressure accumulator so pressure can fall during an ABS or stability cycle, then closes for reapply.
c: Outlet valve coil open or shorted

C001A.d: Set when the ABS modulator cannot release pressure at the left rear wheel within the expected time during a control cycle, the left rear equivalent of C0012 and C0016. After the module commands the left rear outlet valve to dump pressure it expects wheel speed to recover and line pressure to fall; a release that exceeds the calibrated time limit indicates a sticking valve, a restricted hydraulic path or an accumulato
s: Extended or firm pedal during hard braking
c: Restricted hydraulic path or contaminated fluid
Pump or accumulator cannot accept fluid

C001C.d: Covers the right rear inlet (apply) solenoid valve of the ABS hydraulic modulator, the right rear counterpart of C0010 and C0018. The module closes this valve to isolate the right rear brake circuit and hold wheel pressure during ABS, traction or stability control, then opens it to reapply pressure; on the rear axle the same channel often supports electronic brake-force distribution.
c: Inlet valve coil open or shorted

C001D.d: Covers the right rear outlet (release) solenoid valve of the ABS hydraulic modulator, the release counterpart to inlet valve C001C. It opens to dump brake fluid from the right rear caliper or wheel cylinder into the low-pressure accumulator so pressure can fall during an ABS or stability cycle, then closes for reapply.
c: Outlet valve coil open or shorted

C001E.d: Set when the ABS modulator cannot release pressure at the right rear wheel within the expected time during a control cycle, completing the per-wheel set with C0012, C0016 and C001A. After commanding the right rear outlet valve to dump pressure the module expects wheel speed to recover and line pressure to fall; a release longer than the calibrated limit points to a sticking valve, a restricted hydraulic path or an ac
s: Extended or firm pedal during hard braking
c: Restricted hydraulic path or contaminated fluid
Pump or accumulator cannot accept fluid

C0020.d: Covers the electric pump (return) motor of the ABS hydraulic unit and its control circuit. The motor drives the piston pump that returns brake fluid from the low-pressure accumulators and builds pressure for ABS, traction and stability interventions.
s: ABS, traction and stability control disabled
c: Pump motor seized or windings failed
Open or shorted motor supply or ground

C0021.d: A performance code for the power brake booster, set when the booster does not deliver the expected level of assist or does not respond to the control module as commanded. On vehicles with an electronic or vacuum booster the module compares driver pedal demand, measured boost and the resulting brake pressure, and stores the code when assist is weak, slow or inconsistent.
s: Hard brake pedal and reduced assist
Service brake or reduced power message
ABS or brake warning lamp on
c: Booster worn or not holding vacuum/pressure
Low battery voltage during module programming
Faulty boost or pressure sensor input

C0022.d: C0022 covers the solenoid valve of an electronically controllable brake booster. Patent literature shows a vacuum booster that works in two ways: by the driver's pedal in normal braking, and through a solenoid valve that changes the pressure in an auxiliary chamber so the booster applies the brakes without the pedal.
s: Changed brake pedal effort or feel
ABS or brake warning lamp on

C0023.d: Covers the stop lamp (brake light) control circuit as driven or monitored by the brake or stability control module. Modern ABS/ESC systems can command the stop lamps during autonomous braking events such as traction control, stability control and automatic emergency braking, independent of the driver pressing the pedal, and they monitor the circuit for opens, shorts and lamp-output disagreement.
s: Stop lamps stay on or do not light
ABS or stability warning lamp on
c: Open or shorted stop lamp wiring

C0024.d: Covers the solenoid that generates brake pedal feedback pressure in an electronic or brake-by-wire braking system. Because the driver is hydraulically decoupled during controlled braking, a pedal-feel simulator uses this solenoid to build a controlled counter-pressure so the pedal feels natural.
s: Loss of brake assist, driver messages
ABS or brake warning lamp on

C0025.d: C0025 covers the pressure sensor on the pedal feedback side of a decoupled or brake-by-wire system, the measuring partner of the feedback valve C0024. In such systems the pedal pushes fluid into a pedal feel simulator via a simulator valve the module can open or close, while separate sensors read pressure in the simulator circuit and in the wheel circuit.
s: Loss of brake assist, driver messages
ABS or brake warning lamp on
c: Feedback pressure sensor out of range

C0030.d: Covers the left front tone wheel (reluctor or encoder ring) that the wheel speed sensor reads to measure rotation. This is a signal-plausibility code rather than a sensor circuit fault: the module sees an erratic, noisy or intermittent speed signal consistent with a damaged, contaminated or loose tone ring rather than a sensor electrical failure.

C0031.d: Covers the left front wheel speed sensor and its circuit. The sensor, usually an active Hall-effect type, reports wheel rotation to the ABS/ESC module for anti-lock, traction and stability control and for speed-dependent functions.
c: Open, shorted or chafed sensor wiring

C0032.d: Covers the supply circuit that powers the left front active wheel speed sensor. Active sensors need a regulated voltage from the ABS/ESC module; this code is set when that supply is open, shorted to ground or to another voltage, or is outside the regulated range so the sensor cannot report a valid signal.
s: No wheel speed signal from this corner
c: Open or shorted sensor supply wire
Corroded connector on the supply side

C0033.d: Covers the right front tone wheel (reluctor or encoder ring) read by the right front wheel speed sensor, the mirror of C0030. It is a signal-plausibility code: the module sees an erratic, noisy or intermittent speed signal consistent with a damaged, contaminated or loose tone ring rather than a sensor electrical failure.

C0034.d: Covers the right front wheel speed sensor and its circuit, the mirror of C0031. The active sensor reports wheel rotation to the ABS/ESC module for anti-lock, traction and stability control and speed-dependent functions.
c: Open, shorted or chafed sensor wiring

C0035.d: C0035 reports a fault in the feed that powers the right front active wheel speed sensor, the right-hand partner of C0032. The ABS/ESC module supplies the sensor with a regulated voltage; an open feed, a short to ground or to another voltage, or a supply outside its window leaves the sensor unable to send a speed signal.
s: ABS, traction and stability control disabled
No speed signal from the right front wheel
c: Open or shorted supply wire to the right front sensor
Sensor shorted internally and pulling the supply down
Sensor supply output of the ABS module faulty

C0036.d: Covers the left rear tone wheel (reluctor or encoder ring) read by the left rear wheel speed sensor, the rear-axle counterpart of C0030 and C0033. It is a signal-plausibility code set when the module sees an erratic, noisy or intermittent rear speed signal consistent with a damaged, contaminated or loose tone ring rather than a sensor circuit failure.

C0037.d: Covers the left rear wheel speed sensor and its circuit, the rear-axle counterpart of C0031 and C0034. The active sensor reports rear wheel rotation to the ABS/ESC module for anti-lock, traction and stability control and electronic brake-force distribution.
c: Wheel speed sensor bent or failed
Open, shorted or chafed sensor wiring

C0038.d: Covers the supply circuit that powers the left rear active wheel speed sensor, the rear-axle counterpart of C0032. Active sensors need a regulated voltage from the ABS/ESC module; this code is set when that supply is open, shorted to ground or to another voltage, or outside the regulated range so the sensor cannot produce a valid signal.
s: No wheel speed signal from this corner
c: Open or shorted sensor supply wire
Corroded connector on the supply side

C0039.d: Covers the right rear tone wheel (reluctor or encoder ring) read by the right rear wheel speed sensor, completing the four-corner tone-wheel set with C0030, C0033 and C0036. It is a signal-plausibility code set when the module sees an erratic, noisy or intermittent rear speed signal consistent with a damaged, contaminated or loose tone ring rather than a sensor circuit failure.

C003A.d: Covers the right rear wheel speed sensor and its circuit, completing the four-corner sensor set with C0031, C0034 and C0037. The active sensor reports rear wheel rotation to the ABS/ESC module for anti-lock, traction and stability control and electronic brake-force distribution.
c: Wheel speed sensor bent or failed
Open, shorted or chafed sensor wiring

C003B.d: Covers the supply circuit that powers the right rear active wheel speed sensor, completing the supply set with C0032 and C0038. Active sensors need a regulated voltage from the ABS/ESC module; this code is set when that supply is open, shorted to ground or to another voltage, or outside the regulated range so the sensor cannot produce a valid signal.
s: No wheel speed signal from this corner
c: Open or shorted sensor supply wire
Corroded connector on the supply side

C003C.d: Covers a single rear tone wheel (reluctor or encoder ring) on vehicles that use one combined rear wheel speed signal, for example from a differential or rear axle sensor, rather than separate left and right rear rings. It is a signal-plausibility code set when the module sees an erratic, noisy or intermittent rear speed signal consistent with a damaged, contaminated or loose tone ring rather than a sensor circuit fai
c: Loose or displaced bearing or axle ring

C003D.d: Covers a single rear wheel speed sensor on vehicles that use one combined rear speed signal, for example a rear axle or differential-mounted sensor, instead of separate left and right rear sensors. It reports rear rotation to the ABS/ESC module for anti-lock, traction and stability control and electronic brake-force distribution.
c: Open, shorted or chafed sensor wiring

C003E.d: Covers the supply circuit that powers a single rear active wheel speed sensor on vehicles with one combined rear speed signal. Active sensors need a regulated voltage from the ABS/ESC module; this code is set when that supply is open, shorted to ground or another voltage, or outside the regulated range so the sensor cannot produce a valid signal.
c: Open or shorted sensor supply wire
Corroded connector on the supply side

C003F.d: A correlation code set when the directional information from the wheel speed sensors does not agree across wheels or with other motion inputs. Directional (bidirectional) wheel speed sensors tell the ABS/ESC module whether a wheel turns forward or backward, which the module uses for hill-hold, rollback detection and stability functions.
c: Damaged tone ring giving false direction

C0040.d: C0040 reports a fault on brake pedal switch A, the first of two switch signals that tell the brake, engine and transmission modules the pedal is pressed. Mazda defines C0040:24 as a circuit malfunction of brake switch signal no.
s: Stop lamps stay on or do not light
Vehicle will not shift out of park
c: Brake switch out of adjustment (Mazda SA-062-23)
Water or corrosion in the battery junction box (Ford TSB 22-2044)

C0041.d: Covers brake pedal switch B, the redundant second brake switch used to cross-check brake pedal switch A. The two switches change state in a defined pattern as the pedal is applied; the module compares them and sets this code when switch B is stuck, open, shorted or disagrees with switch A.
s: Driver-assist features disabled or false triggers
Cruise or adaptive cruise will not set

C0042.d: Covers circuit A of the brake pedal position sensor, which reports how far the pedal is pressed rather than just on/off like a switch. The brake or stability module uses this analog signal for brake-by-wire assist, regenerative braking blending and precise stop-lamp and cruise control.
s: ABS or brake warning lamp on
c: Pedal position sensor out of range

C0043.d: Covers circuit B of the brake pedal position sensor, the redundant second channel that the module cross-checks against channel A (C0042). Dual-channel pedal position sensors provide two independent voltage signals, often with opposite slopes, so the module can detect a single-channel fault by correlation.
s: Brake lights stay on or behave oddly
ABS or brake warning lamp on
c: Pedal position sensor channel B out of range
Channel A/B signals do not correlate

C0044.d: Covers brake pressure sensor A (sensor 1) in the ABS/ESC hydraulic unit, which measures master-cylinder or circuit brake pressure. The stability and brake modules use this reading to know how hard the driver is braking and to control traction, stability, brake assist and hill-hold.
s: ABS or brake warning lamp on
c: Pressure sensor failed or out of range
Fault internal to the integrated brake unit

C0045.d: C0045 covers brake pressure sensor B, the second pressure transducer in the ABS/ESC hydraulic unit next to sensor A (C0044). Two sensors let the module watch both brake circuits or check one reading against the other for stability control, brake assist and brake-by-wire functions.
s: ABS or brake warning lamp on
c: Pressure sensor failed or out of range
Fault internal to the integrated brake unit
Signal does not correlate with sensor A

C0046.d: A correlation code for the pair of brake pressure sensors A and B, set when their readings do not agree within the expected tolerance. Where C0044 and C0045 flag a single-sensor electrical fault, this code is a plausibility fault: at the same instant both sensors should report consistent pressure (allowing for their known relationship), and a persistent mismatch indicates one sensor has drifted, a hydraulic fault sep
s: ABS or brake warning lamp on
c: One pressure sensor drifted or biased

C0047.d: Covers the pressure sensor in the power brake booster or brake actuation unit, which measures boost or assist pressure so the module can regulate assist and detect loss of boost. The module monitors the sensor for a signal outside the valid range, an open or short and values that disagree with pedal demand or master-cylinder pressure.
s: Soft or extended pedal at start-up
ABS or brake warning lamp on
c: Booster pressure sensor out of range

C0048.d: Covers the travel (position) sensor of the power brake booster or brake actuation unit, which reports how far the booster input rod or piston has moved so the module can match assist to driver demand. The module monitors the sensor for a signal outside the valid range, an open or short and a position that is implausible against pedal position or boost pressure.
s: ABS or brake warning lamp on
c: Travel sensor out of range or failed

C0049.d: Covers the brake fluid level input to the brake or stability module, used to warn the driver and to disable functions that must not run with low fluid. A float switch or sensor in the master-cylinder reservoir signals when fluid drops below a safe level; the module sets this code and lights the red brake warning indicator.
s: ABS and stability control may be disabled
c: Low fluid from worn pads or a leak
Faulty reservoir level sensor or float

C004A.d: Covers the brake lining (pad) wear sensor circuit, which warns the driver when friction material is worn to its limit. Electronic wear sensors use a loop embedded in the pad that the disc contacts and opens, or a wear-indicator circuit, as the lining wears down; the module reports pad wear and may store this code for an open, shorted or implausible sensor circuit as well as for a genuine worn-pad signal.
s: Possible squeal from a mechanical indicator
c: Brake pads worn to the sensor limit
Open or shorted wear sensor circuit
Sensor not renewed after pad change

C004B.d: Covers an electrical fault, specifically an open or out-of-range circuit, in the brake fluid level sensor or switch, as opposed to C0049 which reports an actual low-level condition. The float switch or level sensor in the reservoir provides a defined signal to the brake or stability module; this code is set when that circuit is open, shorted or gives an implausible value so the module can no longer trust the level re
s: Brake fluid level reads as unknown

C004C.d: Set in an electric or electro-hydraulic brake booster when the position sensor of booster motor A reports a learned reference value outside the allowed adaptation range. The brake control unit learns the rest and travel positions of the motor-driven actuator so it can meter assist precisely; if the learned value drifts beyond the calibrated window the module can no longer trust the actuator position and stores this c
s: ABS or brake warning lamp on
c: Mechanical wear in the booster actuator
Learning routine ran under wrong conditions

C004D.d: A performance code set when the brake system builds or changes hydraulic pressure more slowly than the control unit commands during an assisted or automated braking event. In electronically controlled brake systems the module commands a target pressure and watches the pressure sensor; if the measured pressure lags the demand beyond a calibrated time or rate it concludes the pump, motor, valves or hydraulic path canno
s: Longer pedal travel or delayed assist
ABS or brake warning lamp on
c: Air in the hydraulic system or low fluid

C004E.d: Set when the actuator of a brake system pressure control valve does not move as commanded and appears mechanically stuck. In electronically controlled brake and stability systems a pressure control valve regulates how much hydraulic pressure reaches the wheel circuits; the module commands the valve and checks the resulting pressure against the demand.
s: ABS, traction and stability control disabled
Abnormal brake behaviour on one circuit
ABS or brake warning lamp on
c: Valve actuator stuck by contamination or wear
Corrosion or debris in the valve bore

C004F.d: Set when the ABS/ESC control module or its integrated pump motor reaches a temperature above the safe operating limit. Repeated or prolonged pressure modulation, for example during long downhill ABS use, frequent stability interventions or an electrical fault that keeps the pump running, heats the hydraulic unit and its motor; the module monitors an internal temperature model or sensor and stores this code to protect
s: ABS and stability control temporarily disabled
ABS warning lamp on during the event
c: Stuck valve causing continuous pump run
Pump motor seizing or high friction

C0050.d: A general circuit-malfunction code for the right rear wheel speed sensor, covering an electrical fault not resolved to a more specific sub-type: open circuit, short to power or ground, or a signal that drops out or becomes implausible while driving. The active sensor reports rear wheel rotation to the ABS/ESC module for anti-lock, traction and stability control and electronic brake-force distribution; a chafed or bro
c: Broken or chafed sensor harness wiring

C0051.d: Covers the steering wheel position (steering angle) sensor and its circuit. The sensor reports absolute steering-wheel angle and rate to the ESC module, which combines it with yaw rate, lateral acceleration and wheel speeds to decide when the car is understeering or oversteering.
c: Neutral position not learned after service

C0052.d: Covers signal A of the steering wheel position sensor. Multi-track steering-angle sensors output several phase-shifted signals (A, B, C, D) so the ESC module can reconstruct absolute angle and detect a single bad channel by cross-checking.
c: Steering angle sensor channel A failed

C0053.d: Covers signal B of the steering wheel position sensor, the second of the multi-track channels the ESC module cross-checks against signals A, C and D to reconstruct absolute steering angle. This code is set when channel B is out of range, open, shorted or inconsistent with the other channels.
c: Steering angle sensor channel B failed

C0054.d: Covers signal C of the steering wheel position sensor, the third multi-track channel the ESC module uses with signals A, B and D to reconstruct absolute steering angle and detect a bad channel by cross-checking. This code is set when channel C is out of range, open, shorted or inconsistent with the others.
c: Steering angle sensor channel C failed

C0055.d: Covers signal D of the steering wheel position sensor, the fourth multi-track channel that completes the set with signals A, B and C. The ESC module reconstructs absolute steering angle from all channels and uses their agreement to detect a single faulty track; this code is set when channel D is out of range, open, shorted or inconsistent with the others.
c: Steering angle sensor channel D failed

C0056.d: Covers an intermittent fault in the left rear wheel speed sensor circuit, where the signal is lost or corrupted only part of the time rather than permanently. The ABS/ESC module expects a clean pulse train proportional to wheel speed; a chafed wire that opens over bumps, a loose or corroded connector, a cracked sensor or a contaminated encoder ring can make the signal drop out briefly.

C0060.d: Covers a general fault in the right rear wheel speed sensor circuit. The active sensor feeds rear wheel rotation to the ABS/ESC module for anti-lock, traction and stability control and electronic brake-force distribution; the module monitors the two-wire circuit for opens, shorts to power or ground, out-of-range current and a missing signal while the vehicle moves.
c: Broken or chafed sensor harness wiring

C0061.d: C0061 flags the lateral acceleration signal, which the stability module compares with the value expected from steering angle, yaw rate and speed. The code sets when the signal is out of range, frozen, noisy or implausible against the other inertial channels.
s: Stability control disabled, ESC warning lamp on
MIL on together with ESC and parking brake warnings (FCA)
c: Headlight leveling sensor position not learned after transport (Mazda)
Lateral accelerometer failed or out of range
Sensor cluster loose or shifted on its mount

C0062.d: C0062 flags the longitudinal acceleration signal, the fore-aft reading used for hill hold, grade detection, all-wheel-drive torque split and brake distribution. The module checks it against the change in wheel speed, braking and throttle and against the other inertial channels, and stores the code for a value out of range, frozen, noisy or implausible.
c: Sensor cluster loose or shifted on its mount

C0063.d: C0063 flags the yaw rate signal, the rotation about the vertical axis that stability control compares with a reference built from steering angle, lateral acceleration and speed. A lasting gap means understeer or oversteer, so a corrupt signal would trigger wrong interventions; the module therefore stores the code and stops ESC when the value is out of range, frozen, noisy or implausible.
c: ABS or driver assistance module software (FCA 08-007-23, 08-128-24)
Yaw rate gyro failed or out of range
Sensor cluster loose or shifted on its mount

C0064.d: C0064 covers the roll rate sensor, a gyroscope that measures rotation about the vehicle's longitudinal axis. NHTSA's brake safety study names roll rate among the vehicle dynamics inputs of the ABS/ESC module, and roll stability control uses it, mainly on tall vehicles, to spot the onset of a rollover and counter it with braking and torque reduction.
c: Roll rate gyro failed or out of range
Loose or shifted sensor cluster mounting

C0065.d: C0065 covers the vertical acceleration sensor, which measures up-and-down acceleration of the body. Bosch's inertial measurement unit shows where it lives today: one housing measures the rates of yaw, pitch and roll plus vertical, longitudinal and lateral acceleration and serves several control systems at once.
s: ABS/ESC or suspension warning lamp on
c: Loose or shifted sensor cluster mounting

C0066.d: Public SAE J2012 code lists still mark C0066 as ISO/SAE reserved, and no manufacturer documents the code in a retrievable bulletin or service text. One current code table assigns it to the pitch rate sensor, which fits its place between roll rate (C0064), vertical acceleration (C0065) and the yaw/longitudinal pair (C0069); the title follows that use.
s: ESC or stability warning lamp on
c: Pitch rate gyro failed, drifting or out of range
Sensor cluster loose or tilted on its mount
Harness or connector fault at the sensor cluster

C0069.d: C0069 is a plausibility code for the yaw rate and longitudinal acceleration sensors taken together. When the vehicle brakes in a bend, yaw, longitudinal and lateral motion must stay in a physical relationship; if the two signals keep contradicting each other or the rest of the inertial set, one channel has drifted, both share a fault, or the cluster has shifted on its mount.
c: One inertial channel drifted or biased
Sensor cluster shifted on its mount

C006A.d: C006A covers a combined multi-axis sensor that delivers several motion axes from one device, the integrated form of the separate lateral, longitudinal, vertical, yaw and roll sensors; NHTSA's brake study and Bosch's six-axis IMU describe such units. The module treats the device as a whole and sets C006A for an internal fault, a failed self-test, lost communication or values that disagree across the axes.
c: Internal sensor fault or failed self-test

C006B.d: Set when the stability or traction control system has been intervening continuously for longer than the calibrated maximum. ESC and traction control are meant to act in short bursts; if the controller keeps modulating brakes or reducing torque beyond a time limit it concludes something is wrong, for example a persistently spinning wheel on ice, a dragging brake, a mismatched tyre or a sensor feeding a wrong signal, a
c: Wheel spinning or slipping for a long time
Wrong sensor input driving the intervention

C006C.d: A general stability-system fault code covering the electronic stability control function as a whole rather than one named sensor or actuator. The ESC module sets it when an internal self-check fails, when the stability function cannot run because required inputs are missing or inconsistent, or when a system-level plausibility check is violated and no more specific code applies.

C0070.d: Covers the vehicle speed sensor circuit, the source of the overall road-speed signal used by the ABS/ESC module and shared with the speedometer, transmission and other systems. On many vehicles road speed is derived from the wheel speed sensors or a transmission output sensor; this code is set when that speed signal is open, shorted, out of range or implausible against the individual wheel speeds.
c: Open or shorted speed signal wiring
Failed wheel or output speed sensor

C0071.d: Covers the input that tells the ABS/ESC module whether the vehicle is in two- or four-wheel-drive mode. Because four-wheel drive links the axles and changes how wheel speeds relate, the stability and ABS strategy must know the current drive mode; this signal comes from the transfer-case switch, the drive-mode selector or a message from the drivetrain controller.
c: Missing drive-mode message on the bus

C0072.d: Set when the brake or stability module estimates that brake temperature has risen above a safe threshold. Few vehicles measure rotor temperature directly; most run a thermal model that integrates braking force, speed and time to estimate how hot the brakes are, and warn or adapt control when overheating is likely, for example on a long descent.
c: Brakes overheated on a long descent
Implausible input to the thermal model

C0073.d: Covers the delivered-driving-torque signal that the engine or powertrain controller reports to the ABS/ESC module during traction and stability control. To limit wheel spin the stability controller asks the powertrain to reduce torque; it then needs confirmation of how much torque was actually delivered to close the loop.

C0074.d: Covers the requested-driving-torque signal that the ABS/ESC module sends to the powertrain controller during traction and stability control, the counterpart to the delivered-torque signal C0073. When a driven wheel spins the stability controller computes a torque-reduction request and transmits it; this code is set when that request path is faulty, the value is out of range, or the request and the powertrain's respon
c: Fault on the torque request path

C0075.d: A performance code for the brake pedal position input, set when the signal is present but behaves implausibly, for example it does not change as expected, lags, or disagrees with brake pressure and the switch. The stability and brake modules use pedal position to blend regenerative and friction braking and to arm or cancel driver-assist functions.
c: Pedal or switch out of adjustment

C0076.d: Covers the pulse-width-modulated signal used within the traction control interface, for example a PWM torque-request or status line exchanged between the stability and powertrain controllers or driving a traction-related actuator. The module monitors the PWM signal's duty cycle, frequency and presence and sets this code when it is missing, out of range or implausible.
c: PWM signal missing or out of range

C0077.d: Covers a low-tire-pressure indication reaching the ABS/ESC or body module, typically from an indirect tyre-pressure monitoring system that infers pressure from wheel behaviour rather than from in-tyre sensors. An under-inflated tyre has a smaller rolling radius and turns faster, and its vibration spectrum shifts; the system detects this from the ABS wheel speed signals and raises a low-pressure warning.

C0078.d: Covers a tyre-diameter fault or mismatch detected by the ABS/ESC or indirect-TPMS logic. The system learns the rolling diameter of each tyre from wheel speeds at known vehicle speed; a tyre that is a different size, badly worn, or a mismatched spare makes one wheel turn at a different rate, which the module flags as a diameter problem.
s: TPMS or stability warning lamp on
c: Badly worn tyre changing rolling radius
Diameter not relearned after tyre change

C0079.d: Covers the variable-effort (speed-sensitive) power steering function, where steering assist is high at low speed for easy parking and reduced at high speed for stability. The ABS/ESC or steering module uses vehicle speed to command the assist level through a solenoid-controlled hydraulic valve or an electric power-steering actuator.
c: Missing or wrong vehicle speed input

C0080.d: Set when the two front wheel speed signals disagree by more than the allowed amount under conditions where they should match, pointing to a wheel-speed or tyre problem rather than a single open circuit. The ABS/ESC module continuously compares left and right front speeds; a persistent mismatch on a straight road can mean a failing sensor, a damaged tone ring, a mismatched or badly worn tyre or uneven inflation.
c: Mismatched, worn or unevenly inflated tyres
Failing sensor or damaged tone ring

C0081.d: Covers the ABS malfunction indicator (warning lamp) itself as driven or monitored by the ABS/ESC module. The module commands the ABS lamp on for a fault and off when healthy, and monitors the output circuit; this code is set when the lamp circuit is open or shorted, the lamp does not respond, or the commanded and observed states disagree, for example a bulb-check failure or a bus message not reaching the cluster.
s: ABS warning lamp stuck on or off
c: Lamp request not reaching the cluster

C0082.d: Covers the brake system malfunction indicator (red brake warning lamp) as driven or monitored by the brake/stability module. The module commands this lamp for serious brake faults such as low fluid, pressure problems or a control fault, and monitors the output; this code is set when the lamp circuit is open or shorted, the lamp does not respond, or commanded and observed states disagree.
s: Red brake lamp stuck on or off
c: Lamp request not reaching the cluster

C0083.d: Covers the tyre-pressure-monitor indicator (TPMS lamp) as driven or monitored by the responsible module. Regulations distinguish a steady low-pressure warning from a flashing TPMS-malfunction indication; this code concerns the indicator path, set when the TPMS lamp circuit is open or shorted, the lamp does not respond, or the commanded and observed states disagree.
s: TPMS indicator stuck on or flashing
c: TPMS cannot monitor, requests fault lamp

C0084.d: Covers the traction-active indicator, the lamp that flashes to tell the driver traction control is currently intervening, as driven or monitored by the ABS/ESC module. The module flashes this lamp during a traction event and monitors the output circuit; this code is set when the indicator circuit is open or shorted, the lamp does not respond, or commanded and observed states disagree.
s: Traction indicator stuck on or off
c: Lamp request not reaching the cluster

C0085.d: Covers the traction-disable indicator, the lamp that shows traction control has been switched off by the driver or by the system, as driven or monitored by the ABS/ESC module. The module lights this lamp when traction control is disabled and monitors the output; this code is set when the indicator circuit is open or shorted, the lamp does not respond, or commanded and observed states disagree.
s: Traction-off indicator stuck on or off
No feedback when toggling traction control
c: Lamp request not reaching the cluster

C0086.d: Covers the vehicle-dynamics indicator, the lamp that signals the status of the electronic stability / vehicle-dynamics control to the driver, as driven or monitored by the ESC module. The module lights or flashes this lamp for stability status and faults and monitors the output; this code is set when the indicator circuit is open or shorted, the lamp does not respond, or commanded and observed states disagree.
s: Dynamics indicator stuck on or off
c: Lamp request not reaching the cluster

C0089.d: Covers the driver switch that turns traction (or stability) control off, and its circuit to the ABS/ESC module. Pressing the switch tells the module to disable intervention and light the traction-off indicator; this code is set when the switch signal is stuck, implausible, or the circuit is open or shorted, for example a switch that reads permanently pressed or a broken wire.
c: Switch stuck or reads permanently pressed

C008A.d: Covers the traction-control mode selector and its input to the ABS/ESC module, used where the driver can choose among traction/terrain modes such as snow, sand, mud or sport that change the slip targets and intervention strategy. This code is set when the mode signal is stuck, implausible, out of range or the circuit is faulty, so the module cannot tell which mode is selected.
s: System defaults to a safe mode
c: Mode selector signal stuck or implausible

C0090.d: Covers the actuator that engages or modulates the power transfer unit (transfer case / front coupling) in a four- or all-wheel-drive system. On demand the controller drives this actuator, typically an electric motor or an electromagnetic/electro-hydraulic clutch operator, to send torque to the secondary axle.
s: Stuck in one drive mode or 2WD default
c: PTU actuator motor or coil failed

C0091.d: Covers position sensor A of the power transfer unit actuator, which reports how far the transfer-case or coupling actuator has moved so the controller can close the loop on torque split or mode. The controller commands the actuator and reads this sensor to confirm the achieved position; this code is set when the sensor signal is out of range, open, shorted or implausible against the commanded or expected position.
c: Position sensor A failed or out of range

C0092.d: Covers position sensor B of the power transfer unit actuator, the redundant or second-channel position feedback the controller cross-checks against sensor A (C0091). Dual position sensors let the controller detect a single faulty channel and keep metering the AWD coupling safely.
c: Position sensor B failed or out of range
Sensor A/B signals do not correlate

C0093.d: Covers the temperature sensor of the power transfer unit, which lets the controller protect the AWD clutch from overheating. Sustained torque transfer, for example prolonged slip or towing, heats the clutch pack and its fluid; the controller reads this sensor and reduces or opens the coupling when temperature climbs too high.
s: No thermal protection of the coupling
c: Temperature sensor out of range or failed

C0094.d: Covers the temperature sensor of the rear differential unit in an all-wheel-drive system, used to protect the rear drive module and its electronically controlled coupling from overheating. Prolonged torque transfer to the rear axle heats the clutch and fluid; the controller reads this sensor and limits engagement when it gets too hot.
s: No thermal protection of the rear unit
c: Temperature sensor out of range or failed

C0095.d: Covers actuator A of the rear differential unit, which engages or modulates the electronically controlled rear coupling or locking differential in an all-wheel-drive system. The controller drives this actuator, typically a motor-operated clutch operator or an electromagnetic coil, to send or lock torque at the rear axle on demand.
s: Rear axle stuck engaged or open

C0096.d: Covers the data or feedback associated with rear differential actuator A (C0095), as opposed to a plain circuit fault. Where C0095 flags the drive circuit, this code is set when the actuator's reported data, its position, current or status feedback, is missing, out of range or implausible against the command, so the controller cannot confirm what the actuator is doing.
c: Actuator feedback data missing or implausible
Communication fault with the rear module

C0097.d: Covers actuator B of the rear differential unit, the second actuator used on rear drive modules that control two functions, for example torque transfer and a limited-slip or locking element, or that use two coils for redundancy. The controller drives this actuator to engage or modulate the rear coupling; this code is set when the actuator B circuit is open, shorted, out of range or the actuator does not respond.

C0098.d: Covers the data or feedback associated with rear differential actuator B (C0097), as opposed to a plain circuit fault. Where C0097 flags the drive circuit, this code is set when actuator B's reported data, its position, current or status feedback, is missing, out of range or implausible against the command, so the controller cannot confirm what the actuator is doing.
c: Actuator feedback data missing or implausible
Communication fault with the rear module

C0099.d: The title gives actuator A of the rear differential unit three position channels, A to C. That layout matches the way brushless actuator motors track their rotor: three Hall elements on the stator read a magnet on the rotor, and their combined states step the motor through six commutation phases.
s: AWD/4WD warning lamp or message in the cluster
Rear axle no longer driven, front-wheel drive only
c: Open or grounded signal wire of channel A between actuator and module
Corroded or loose connector at the rear drive unit
Failed Hall element A inside the actuator motor
Missing sensor supply or ground from the module

C009A.d: Channel B is the second of the three position signals that actuator A of the rear differential unit reports to its control module. This code points at that one line or element, while channels A and C still deliver plausible edges.
s: AWD warning with the vehicle driving on the front axle only
Fault may come and go with temperature or vibration
c: Damaged or chafed signal wire of channel B
Loose or spread terminal for channel B in the actuator connector
Hall element B in the actuator motor defective

C009B.d: C009B covers the third position channel, C, of actuator A in the rear differential unit. With A and B intact the module can still see motion, so a fault on C is caught by comparing edges: a Woodward patent identifies the failed sensor as the one whose output stays constant between two invalid state combinations, roughly one electrical revolution apart, and then keeps the motor running on two sensors with a synthesise
s: All-wheel drive switched off for the rest of the trip
c: Open circuit or short on the channel C signal line
Hall element C inside the actuator motor failed
Moisture in the actuator connector at the rear axle

C009C.d: Each of the three position channels of actuator A may look electrically fine, yet together they make no sense: a combination that cannot occur, a sequence that skips states or runs against the commanded direction. With 120-degree spacing the patterns 000 and 111 are invalid, as a Woodward patent notes.
s: 4WD Malfunction message and AWD switched off
Service AdvanceTrac, hill start assist or pre-collision assist unavailable (Ford)
c: Rear drive unit connector not fully seated or loose pins (Ford C413)
Poor shared sensor ground or supply corrupting all three channels
Internal sensor or magnet fault in the rear drive unit motor

C009D.d: Actuator B exists only on rear units with a second controlled element, for instance twin-clutch modules that apply torque to each rear wheel on its own, or a rear axle with an extra disconnect. GKN describes a separate actuator controller managing such twin-clutch actuation, adapting to clutch temperature and wear.
s: AWD warning, torque vectoring or locking function unavailable
Vehicle may push wide in corners where it normally rotates
c: Wiring fault on channel A of actuator B
Poor contact in the actuator B connector
Hall element A in actuator B failed

C009E.d: Middle channel B of the second rear-unit actuator is reported here. It belongs to designs with two independently controlled elements; GKN's Twinster, used on the Focus RS rear drive module, can send torque to either rear wheel separately through two wet clutches.
s: AWD fault message, one rear wheel no longer driven actively
Drift or sport drive modes unavailable
c: Channel B signal of actuator B interrupted or grounded
Harness chafed near the rear axle or exhaust heat shield
Internal sensor failure in actuator B

C009F.d: Third position channel C of actuator B in the rear differential unit is the subject of this code. Its absence is noticed because the remaining channels A and B still produce transitions that C should follow.
s: Rear torque split or locking function deactivated
c: Open or high-resistance channel C line of actuator B
Hall element C of actuator B defective
Fault in electronics integrated in the actuator motor

C00A0.d: C00A0 is the plausibility check across all three position channels of actuator B. Each line may be intact, but the pattern they form is impossible, out of sequence or contradicts the commanded movement, so the controller can no longer trust where the second actuator stands.
s: AWD fault message with rear torque control switched off
Possible loss of related assist functions shown in the cluster
c: Shared sensor ground or supply of actuator B faulty
Actuator B connector not fully latched
Rotor magnet or sensor carrier shifted inside actuator B

C00A1.d: This umbrella code concerns the driveline control module itself, often called AWD or 4WD module, not one of its outputs or sensors. It covers internal faults such as memory or processor errors, a missing or poor supply and ground, or software and configuration problems that stop the module from controlling clutches, transfer case or disconnects.
s: Further driveline codes or lost communication with the module
c: Loose or corroded module ground (Ford G239 on 2023 Super Duty)
Low battery voltage or poor supply to the module
Module software or configuration fault, update or reprogramming needed
Internal failure of the driveline control module

C00A2.d: The power transfer unit sits at the front transaxle of a front-based AWD car and, on disconnecting systems, can uncouple the propshaft. AAM's EcoTrac, introduced on the 2014 Jeep Cherokee, separates the driveline at both the PTU and the rear module under command of its own control unit.
s: AWD unavailable, vehicle stays in front-wheel drive
c: Short to ground or battery on the PTU actuator circuit
PTU actuator coil or motor open or internally shorted
Damaged output stage inside the driveline module

C00A3.d: C00A3 points to the driver stage inside the driveline module that powers actuator A of the rear differential unit, not to the actuator itself. The module's own transistor monitoring reports something wrong at that output.
s: AWD warning in the instrument cluster
c: Short to ground or battery in the actuator A supply lines
Actuator A motor or coil drawing excessive current (binding, winding short)
Output stage in the module overheated or defective

C00A4.d: Where a rear unit carries a second actuator, for example the second clutch of a twin-clutch module that can drive each rear wheel on its own, the driveline module needs a second output stage, and C00A4 reports a fault in that one. If actuator B is a brushless motor, the stage is a three-phase bridge: automotive gate drivers such as TI's DRV8343-Q1 detect short to battery, short to ground, MOSFET overcurrent and gate
s: One rear clutch or locking function inactive
c: Phase or supply line of actuator B shorted to ground or battery
Winding fault or blocked rotor in actuator B causing overcurrent
Failed output stage B in the module

C00A5.d: C00A5 concerns the output stage in the driveline module that powers the transfer case actuator, typically a DC gearmotor that shifts range and mode or presses a multi-plate clutch. Bosch describes such a transfer case clutch driven by a DC motor with worm gear through an H-bridge, with motor speed, worm wheel position and motor current measured; Magna's shift patent regulates the gearmotor speed by PWM and switches t
s: 4WD/AWD cannot be engaged or range shift refused
c: Shorted transfer case motor wiring or connector
Binding or worn transfer case motor causing overcurrent
Defective H-bridge in the driveline module

C00A6.d: C00A6 is the general code for the transfer case actuator, the motor unit that presses the transfer case clutch or moves its shift mechanism. Ford uses it with many failure-type suffixes.
s: Wrench (powertrain malfunction) indicator or AWD lamp (Ford)
c: Harness to the actuator motor chafed on the underbody heat shield
Front axle disconnect actuator/intermediate shaft fault (Ford Explorer/Aviator)
Transfer case clutch actuator motor worn or seized

C00A7.d: Position sensor A reports where the transfer case actuator, and thus the range or mode mechanism, currently stands. Magna patents a linear Hall sensor bolted from outside into the case, reading a stepped sector plate (four positions over about 60 degrees) or a plate on the range fork, with a duty-cycle output.
s: 4WD Service light or 4WD Fault Service Required message
c: Transfer case shift motor connector not fully seated (Stellantis 2023)
Harness chafed where it routes to the actuator motor (Ford)
Position sensor A in the actuator failed

C00A8.d: C00A8 is the second position signal of the transfer case actuator. Whether B is a redundant copy of A or tracks a different part, the motor or the cam, is not published by any maker; BorgWarner, for example, puts a contact probe on the shift drum cam instead of the motor because a torsion spring sits in between, and reads five plateaus from 2WD high to 4WD low.
s: 4WD Service light, four-wheel drive not available
c: Harness damage at the heat shield near the transfer case (Ford)
